items.en: Muscle-strengthening activities should be done involving major muscle groups (legs, back, abdomen, chest, shoulders and arms), on 2 or more days a week.

items.zh: 中醫學強調，適當的運動可以調暢經絡，疏通氣血，調節人體的陰陽平衡。若缺乏足夠的運動，容易導致氣滯血瘀，增加疾病風險。適當接觸陽光、曬太陽可以起到溫通全身經絡，振奮陽氣的作用， 因此適當在陽光下進行的戶外運動可以提振身心活力，對身體健康產生如：祛除體內的寒濕之氣，以及強化體質、增強抵抗力等諸多益處。
items.en: Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) emphasizes that appropriate exercise can regulate the meridians, promote the smooth circulation of qi and blood, and harmonize the body's yin and yang balance. Inadequate exercise can easily result in qi stagnation and blood stasis, increasing the risk of disease. Proper exposure to sunlight helps warm and unblock the meridians throughout the body and invigorate yang qi. Therefore, engaging in outdoor exercise under temperate sunlight revitalizes both physical and mental well-being, providing numerous health benefits such as dispelling pathogenic dampness and cold, reinforcing our body constitution, and boosting immunity.

items.label: 在選擇運動類型時，亦應考量個人的體質差異。對於畏寒怕冷、四肢冰冷，或身體沉重困倦、舌苔厚膩的人士，可適度提高戶外陽光下運動頻率，溫和的日曬有助於
items.zh: 在選擇運動類型時，亦應考量個人的體質差異。對於畏寒怕冷、四肢冰冷，或身體沉重困倦、舌苔厚膩的人士，可適度提高戶外陽光下運動頻率，溫和的日曬有助於幫助讓身體溫陽散寒、化解身體的濕氣。相反， 陰虛内熱或濕熱體質者（如容易口乾咽乾、心煩、易長暗瘡粉刺），則需謹慎，過度曝曬於陽光下可能會傷津耗液，加重身體本身的症狀。正因如此，本身患有高血壓或皮膚敏感的人士亦應多加留意，避免過度曝曬。如想確保能選擇適合自身體質的運動，建議咨詢中醫師醫囑進行調整。
items.en: When choosing the type of exercise, individual differences in body constitution should also be considered. For individuals who are averse to cold, have cold hands and feet, often feel heavy and fatigued, or have thick, slimy tongue fur, moderately increasing the frequency of outdoor exercise in the sun is recommended. For gentle sunlight helps warm yang, dispel cold, and resolve bodily dampness.

items.label: Conversely, individuals with yin deficiency with internal heat or damp-h
items.en: Conversely, individuals with yin deficiency with internal heat or damp-heat constitutions (e.g., those prone to dry mouth and throat, irritability, or frequent acne breakouts) should proceed with caution, as excessive sun exposure can deplete fluids and worsen existing symptoms. It is for the same reason that individuals with hypertension or sensitive skin should take extra care in how much sunlight they expose to themselves as well. To ensure that the exercises chosen are suitable for your constitution, consultation with a Chinese medicine practitioner is recommended.

items.zh: 中醫養生講究平衡之道，過猶不及。因此，一般建議在初日出或陽光溫和時進行戶外運動，而非在烈日當空、酷熱難耐之時。在陽光下運動時應避免過度曝曬；運動強度以「微微出汗」為宜，切忌大汗淋漓，以致損傷身體的精氣與津液，防止過度體力消耗導致的元氣損傷 。
items.en: TCM health preservation emphasizes the principle of balance—excess is just as harmful as deficiency. Therefore, it is generally recommended to engage in outdoor exercise during early morning sunrise or when the sunlight is mild, rather than under the scorching midday sun. Excessive sun exposure should be avoided during exercise. Ideally, one exercises to induce "light sweating" rather than profuse sweating, which can deplete the body's essential qi and fluids. This practice prevents damage to the original qi caused by overexertion.

items.label: 運動的適宜強度與時長亦應隨四季更迭而調整, 順應四季”春生，夏長，秋收，冬藏“的規律1。夏季陽氣升發 ，氣候由溫轉熱，宜順應生發之勢，適度增加戶
items.zh: 運動的適宜強度與時長亦應隨四季更迭而調整, 順應四季”春生，夏長，秋收，冬藏“的規律1。夏季陽氣升發 ，氣候由溫轉熱，宜順應生發之勢，適度增加戶外活動；但夏季炎熱時應避開烈日高溫，選擇清晨或傍晚進行和緩運動，以微微出汗為度，以助去除體内濕氣。在寒冷的秋冬季節，陽氣漸收，陰氣漸盛，則應適度降低日常運動強度，順應自然以收斂陽氣，固藏陰精。
items.en: The appropriate intensity and duration of exercise should also be adjusted according to the changing seasons, following the natural rhythm: "Sow in spring, develop in summer, harvest in autumn, and store in winter1." In summertime, as yang qi rises and the weather turns from warm to hot, one should align with the rising momentum of yang qi by moderately increasing outdoor activities. However, in the heat of summer, one should avoid the intense sunlight. Opt for early morning or evening gentle exercises that induce light sweating, helping to dispel internal dampness. In autumn and winter when it grows cold, yang qi gradually recedes and yin qi flourishes in turn. Daily exercise intensity should be moderately reduced to follow nature's cycle of restraining yang qi and storing yin essence.

items.zh:
手機應用程式簡介

戶外健體設施手機應用程式

香港自2002年開始在戶外設置適合長者使用的戶外健體設施。2016年開始，為配合活齡城市發展的願景及加強居家安老配套設施，香港政府加大力度在各地區設置更多的戶外健體設施。本地研究顯示這些設施提供了獨特的平台給于不同身體狀況的長者在社區保持恆常運動習慣，促進身心健康。

在社區，已經有一部份長者懂得好好利用戶外健體設施協助自己維持恆常運動習慣，也有一部份長者並不認識這些健體設施亦不懂得如何安全有效地使用。有見及此，香港理工大學康復治療科學系的專家團隊為每一部戶外健體設施編寫了更詳細的介紹，為每一部運動器材增加了康復科學角度提醒使用者如何安全及有效地使用這些設施，亦增加了“給照顧者的提示”部份，希望照顧者如果帶同長者去使用設施時會提點及觀察他們的運動姿勢及使用方法是否正確，以提升運動儀器使用的安全及有效程度。

我們希望程式的內容能夠協助長者安全及有效地使用設施，增加日常活動量以提升生活自理能力及提升生活質素。

李樂真博士
首席研究員
items.en:
Mobile Apps for Outdoor Exercise Facilities

The Hong Kong government has been installing outdoor exercise facilities for older adults since 2002. And starting from 2016, the Government has stepped up its efforts to provide more outdoor exercise facilities across the territory to meet the vision of an age-friendly city and enhance the supporting facilities for seniors. Local studies have shown that outdoor fitness facilities provide a unique platform for older adults with different physical conditions to maintain regular exercise habits and promote physical and mental health.

Some older adults in the community have already used the outdoor exercise facilities to help them maintain regular exercise habits, yet most of them do not know how to utilise the facilities safely and effectively. In view of this, a team of experts from the Department of Rehabilitation Sciences of The Hong Kong Polytechnic University rescripted a more detailed introduction and explanation of benefits on each outdoor exercise equipment. In addition, the perspective of rehabilitation science is added to each equipment to educate users to utilise the facilities safely and effectively. The team have also prepared a section for caregivers with advice and reminders on correct postures and proper usage. When caregivers accompany older adults to use these outdoor exercise facilities, they can help to observe and remind older adult users to exercise with correct posture and use the equipment properly. This will enhance the safety and effective use of outdoor exercise equipment.

The contents in the apps could assist older adults to utilise the facilities safely and effectively. Improvement in daily physical activity level will enhance their self-care ability, level of independence, as well as improving quality of life.

Dr Janet Lee
Principal Investigator

items.label: 經常進行體能活動不但有益身心，而且樂趣無窮，因此，愈來愈多人開始每天多做運動。對大部分人來說，多做運動是很安全的。不過，有些人則應在增加運動量前
items.zh:
經常進行體能活動不但有益身心，而且樂趣無窮，因此，愈來愈多人開始每天多做運動。對大部分人來說，多做運動是很安全的。不過，有些人則應在增加運動量前，先行徵詢醫生的意見。

如果你計劃增加運動量，請先回答下列7條問題。如果你介乎15至69歲之間，這份體能活動適應能力問卷會告訴你應否在開始前諮詢醫生。如果你超過69歲及沒有經常運動，請徵詢醫生的意見。

普通常識是回答這些問題的最佳指引。請仔細閱讀下列問題，然後誠實回答（請答「是」或「否」）：

1. 醫生曾否說過你的心臟有問題，以及只可進行醫生建議的體能活動？

2. 你進行體能活動時會否感到胸口痛？

3. 過去一個月內，你曾否在沒有進行體能活動時也感到胸口痛？

4. 你曾否因感到暈眩而失去平衡，或曾否失去知覺？

5. 你的骨骼或關節(例如脊骨、膝蓋或髖關節)是否有毛病，且會因改變體能活動而惡化？

6. 醫生現時是否有開血壓或心臟藥物（例如 water pills）給你服用？

7. 是否有其他理由令你不應進行體能活動？
items.en:
Regular physical activity is fun and healthy, and increasingly more people are starting to become more active every day. Being more active is very safe for most people. However, some people should check with their doctor before they start becoming much more physically active.

If you are planning to become much more physically active than you are now, start by answering the seven questions in the box below. If you are between the ages of 15 and 69, the PAR-Q will tell you if you should check with your doctor before you start. If you are over 69 years of age, and you are not used to being very active, check with your doctor.

Common sense is your best guide when you answer these questions. Please read the questions carefully and answer each one honestly (YES or NO).

1. Has your doctor ever said that you have a heart condition and that you should only do physical activity recommended by a doctor?

2. Do you feel pain in your chest when you do physical activity?

3. In the past month, have you had chest pain when you were not doing physical activity?

4. Do you lose your balance because of dizziness or do you ever lose consciousness?

5. Do you have a bone or joint problem (for example, back, knee or hip) that could be made worse by a change in your physical activity?

6. Is your doctor currently prescribing drugs (for example, water pills) for your blood pressure or heart condition?

7. Do you know of any other reason why you should not do physical activity?

items.label: 如果你對這份問卷的全部問題誠實地答「否」，你有理由確信你可以：
items.zh:
如果你對這份問卷的全部問題誠實地答「否」，你有理由確信你可以：

開始增加運動量──開始時慢慢進行，然後逐漸增加，這是最安全和最容易的方法。

參加體能評估──這是一種確定你基本體能的好方法，以便你擬定最佳的運動計劃。此外，亦主張你量度血壓；如果讀數超過144/94，請先徵詢醫生的意見，然後才逐漸增加運動量。

延遲增加運動量：

如果你因傷風或發燒等暫時性疾病而感到不適──請在康復後才增加運動量。

如果你懷孕或可能懷孕──請先徵詢醫生的意見，然後才決定是否增加運動量。
items.en:
If you answered NO honestly to all PAR-Q questions, you can be reasonably sure that you can:

Start becoming much more physically active – begin slowly and build up gradually. This is the safest and easiest way to go.

Take part in a fitness appraisal – this is an excellent way to determine your basic fitness so that you can plan the best way for you to live actively. It is also highly recommended that you have your blood pressure evaluated. If your reading is over 144/94, talk with your doctor before you start becoming much more physically active.

DELAY BECOMING MUCH MORE ACTIVE:

If you are not feeling well because of a temporary illness such as a cold or a fever – wait until you feel better; or

If you are or may be pregnant – talk to your doctor before you start becoming more active.

items.label: 在開始增加運動量或進行體能評估前，請先致電或親身與醫生商談，告知醫生這份問卷，以及你回答「是」的問題。
items.zh:
在開始增加運動量或進行體能評估前，請先致電或親身與醫生商談，告知醫生這份問卷，以及你回答「是」的問題。

你可以進行任何活動，但須在開始時慢慢進行，然後逐漸增加活動量；又或你只可進行一些安全的活動。告訴醫生你希望參加的活動及聽從他的意見。你可以找出一些安全及有益健康的社區活動。
items.en:
Talk with your doctor by phone or in person BEFORE you start becoming much more physically active or BEFORE you have a fitness appraisal. Tell your doctor about this questionnaire and which questions you answered YES.

You may be able to do any activity you want — as long as you start slowly and build up gradually. Or, you may need to restrict your activities to those which are safe for you. Talk with your doctor about the kinds of activities you wish to participate in and follow his/her advice.

Find out which community programs are safe and helpful for you.

items.label: 在使用戶外健身設備時的安全注意事項
items.zh:
在使用戶外健身設備時的安全注意事項

以下是康樂及文化事務署提供的一般安全指南：

1. 長者健身角裡的所有健身設備都應該以規律和適當的節奏使用。如果有疑問，請事先諮詢醫療專業人士。

2. 在使用健身設備之前應進行10至15分鐘的熱身，然後在使用後進行8至10分鐘的緩和運動。

3. 在飢餓或吃飽的狀態下請勿進行運動。宜於餐後1至1½小時才進行劇烈運動。另外，避免在運動前飲酒。

4. 請穿著舒適透氣的衣服和平底運動鞋。

5. 為避免因誤用健身器材而受傷，使用前請先仔細閱讀器材的操作說明。

6. 使用健身器材前，請確保其運作正常。如果發現器材運作不正常或出現故障，請立即通知公園工作人員。請勿自行嘗試修理。

7. 注意您的身體狀況和限制。如果感覺不適，請立即停止運動並向公園內的工作人員或他人尋求幫助。

跌倒風險管理

在室外鍛煉可為健康帶來益處，然而，需要注意的是戶外可能會有增加跌倒風險的因素，例如不平坦的路面，石壆或雜物等可能導致跌倒的障礙物，光線不足或惡劣的天氣狀況等。

我們可以做些什麼來減少在空外活動時跌倒的風險？

1. 穿上有防滑坑紋的運動鞋。

2. 避免在光線不足的環境中使用設備 （以免未注意到地面上的物件）。

3. 感覺不適時立即坐下。

4. 謹慎地行走和使用設備。

5. 使用設備前先檢查其狀況。

6. 帶上一個同行者陪伴。

7. 留意環境轉變，例如天氣及路況。
items.en:
Safety precautions when we using outdoor exercise equipment

Below are the general safety guidelines suggested by the Leisure and Cultural Services Department:

1. All the fitness equipment in the Corner should be used at regular and appropriate pace. If in doubt, consult a medical professional beforehand.

2. Warm up for 10 to 15 minutes before using the fitness equipment and do 8 to 10 minutes of cool-down afterwards.

3. Do not exercise when you are hungry or full. Wait 1 to 1½ hours after meal before doing any strenuous exercise. Do not drink alcohol before exercise.

4. Wear comfortable and air-permeable clothes and flat-heeled sports shoes.

5. To prevent injury due to misuse of the fitness equipment, read the operation instructions carefully before using it.

6. Make sure the fitness equipment functions properly before using it. If it does not work properly or is out of order, inform the staff in the park immediately.Do not attempt to fix it yourself.

7. Pay attention to your physical condition and limitations. If you feel unwell, stop exercising immediately and seek help from the staff or others in the park.

Fall risk management

Exercising at outdoor gives health benefits, however, one should note that outdoor environment increase risk of falls due to reasons like uneven walking surfaces, fall hazards like curbs or clutter, poor lighting or inclement weather. 

What can we do to reduce risk of falling in the outdoor environment?

1. Put on slippery-proof footwears.

2. Avoid using the equipment in the dark (Not noticing objects on the floor).

3. Take a seat immediate when feeling unwell.

4. Walk and use the equipment with care.

5. Check the equipment before stepping on it and using it.

6. Bring a companion.

7. Be aware to any changes in the environment, such as the weather and the road condition.

items.label: S - 具體（Specific）：清楚說明要做什麼，例如「在公園步行」。
items.zh:
S - 具體（Specific）：清楚說明要做什麼，例如「在公園步行」。
M - 可量度（Measurable）：加入數字，例如「每次30分鐘，每週3次」。
A - 可達成（Achievable）：設定在自己能力範圍內的目標。
R - 相關（Relevant）：目標應與你的健康有關。
T - 有時限（Time-bound）：設定時間範圍，例如「本週內」。

例子：「本週一、三、五在公園使用健身單車各20分鐘。」
items.en:
S - Specific: state clearly what you will do, e.g. "walk in the park".
M - Measurable: include numbers, e.g. "30 minutes, 3 times a week".
A - Achievable: set a goal within your current ability.
R - Relevant: the goal should matter to your health.
T - Time-bound: set a time frame, e.g. "this week".

Example: "This week I will use the fitness bike in the park for 20 minutes on Monday, Wednesday and Friday."
